full_judgment: 15. We have noticed in both the cases that the defendant government has failed to prove that the required show cause notices were ever served on and received by the owners of the suit lands. We have also noted from the record that the defendant Government has also been unsuccessful in proving possession in the suit land in the leave petition. Since sections 7 and 11 are designed to divest the owners of the suit lands of their ownership and possession in the suit lands the same should be strictly interpreted and applied. The defendant Government has failed to discharge its burden of proof that the suit lands were taken over and vested in the Forest Department of the Government by issuing required show cause notices on the owners of the suit lands inviting objection and on due consideration of the objections, if any, raised by the owners: The learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the Government submits that since the defendant Government has succeeded in producing the Gazette Notifications issued under sections 7 and 11 of the Private Forests Act, 1945 the Government should be taken to have issued necessary show cause notices on the owners of the suit lands inviting objection and taken over and vested the suit lands in the Forest Department in due consideration of the objections of the owners of the suit lands, even in the absence of any such notices having been produced and proved before the Court. We do not find force in this contention. In both the cases Courts below have found on evidence that the lands taken over by the aforesaid Gazette notifications were not the category of lands liable to be taken over and vested in the Forest Department under the law. The said notifications are therefore ultra vires the law. We are therefore of the view that the taking over and vesting of the suit lands covered by the aforesaid Civil Appeal and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal were not made in due compliance of the mandatory requirements under sections 7 and 11 of the Private Forests Act, 1945. In this view of the matter, the taking over and vesting of the suit lands in the Forest Department by the Government by the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 3-6-1958 and 3-9-1953 in the aforesaid appeal and the leave petition respectively have not been proved and they remain merely as a paper transaction.
